record.paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: new narrowband reference signals for NTN positioning
record.original_question: What reference-signal design should 3GPP standardize for non-terrestrial-network (NTN) positioning so that user equipment does not need power-intensive wideband positioning reference signal (PRS) searches across multi-subframe windows, Doppler measurements are supported, and transmission/reception points and user equipment can maintain phase coherence over a new narrowband PRS spanning multiple slots?

evidence.quote: New Reference Signal Design. Another shortcoming with the current positioning process is the need for the UE to search for a wideband PRS within a specific time search window. In TNs, where distances between UE and TRPs are smaller, this window is shorter than a subframe duration. However, in NTN setups with larger relative distances between reference and neighboring TRPs, the search window expands across multiple subframes. For UEs, extended searches for wideband signals can be power-intensive.

Designing quasi-co-located narrow-band synchronization signals, akin to synchronization signal blocks, alongside PRS in a deterministic manner might be advantageous. To enable Doppler measurements, 3GPP needs to standardize new narrowband PRS, with resources defined over multiple slots. The TRP and the UE need to maintain phase coherence over the transmission of this signal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cellular positioning system in which a user equipment (UE) estimates its location from downlink positioning reference signals (PRS) transmitted by multiple transmission/reception points (TRPs). In a non-terrestrial-network (NTN) setting, the TRPs are mounted on satellites (e.g., in low Earth orbit), so that (i) propagation delays between the reference TRP and neighboring TRPs differ by amounts spanning multiple OFDM subframes, (ii) line-of-sight relative motion produces large, time-varying Doppler shifts, and (iii) maintaining radio-frequency phase coherence between TRP transmitters and the UE receiver across long observation intervals is nontrivial.

A conventional wideband PRS forces the UE to perform a correlation search over a time window of multiple subframes, which is power-intensive. The problem is to design a new downlink reference-signal scheme, suitable for standardization, with the following requirements:

1. The signal includes narrowband synchronization blocks that are quasi-co-located with the PRS in a deterministic time-frequency pattern, so that the UE can acquire timing and frequency without a wideband multi-subframe search.

2. The signal is a narrowband PRS whose resources are deployed over multiple slots in such a way that the UE can produce reliable Doppler (carrier-frequency-offset / Doppler rate) measurements in addition to time-of-arrival measurements.

3. The TRP transmitter and UE receiver are required to maintain phase coherence across the entire multi-slot transmission of the new narrowband PRS, enabling coherent combining across slots.

Specify the time-frequency resource mapping, sequence design, quasi-co-location structure, and phase-coherence requirements of such a reference signal, and analyze its time-of-arrival, Doppler, and phase-estimation performance (e.g., via Cramér–Rao bounds) under NTN-typical delay, Doppler, and oscillator-stability conditions, demonstrating that it simultaneously satisfies (1)–(3) while improving on a wideband multi-subframe PRS search.
artifact.status_search_result: 3GPP has continued evolving NR positioning (Releases 17–18) and NB-IoT/eMTC NTN support, but a standardized narrowband PRS for NTN that supplies Doppler measurements with multi-slot phase coherence and quasi-co-located synchronization blocks is not yet specified. Recent surveys on LEO-based 6G positioning explicitly list limited phase coherence and high Doppler variability as open signal-design challenges, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: LEO-based Positioning: Foundations, Signal Design, and Receiver Enhancements for 6G NTN
status_evidence.snippet: limited phase coherence hinders coherent combining of signals across time, and high variability in delay and Doppler shifts adds additional complexity in detecting and tracking PRS signals.
status_evidence.claim: Phase-coherent, Doppler-robust narrowband PRS design for NTN is identified as an open challenge in recent 6G NTN positioning literature.

status_evidence.title: 5G Advanced positioning in 3GPP Release 18 - Ericsson
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of Release 18 positioning enhancements, focused on terrestrial improvements; NTN-specific narrowband PRS with multi-slot phase coherence is not part of the finalized standard.
status_evidence.claim: As of Release 18, 3GPP has not standardized an NTN-specific narrowband PRS satisfying the stated requirements.
